Kata

Build a coding-agent harness in Go, with a grader that tells you what is broken.

Read it online at kata.akhand.cc.

Kata is a course of eleven chapters and one local tool. You write the harness: the provider client, the tools, the loop, sessions, the context budget, steering, skills, subagents, and an MCP client. The tool runs your code against a scripted model and reports which claim failed and why.

git clone <this repo> && cd kata
go build -o kata ./cmd/kata

./kata                 # where you are, what to do next
./kata read 01         # the task for chapter 01
./kata submit 01       # compile, grade, report

No account, no API key, no Docker, no network after the clone.

Why a grader

A harness sits around a model that is random, slow, and paid for. That makes the obvious teaching method, "run it and see", useless: the answer changes each time and a failure costs money.

Kata replaces the model with a scripted HTTP server and keeps the wire. You speak real Server-Sent Events to a real socket. Only the reply is fixed. So every check is instant, offline, and byte-precise, and a failure names the mechanism rather than showing a diff of prose.

  FAIL 04 surfaces a non-2xx response as *agent.HTTPError
        why: A 429 is not a parse failure. Wrapping it in a typed error is
             what lets the loop later retry with backoff.
        field: error type
        expected: "*agent.HTTPError"
        actual:   provider: HTTP 429: {"error":"slow down"}
        hint: Check resp.StatusCode before you touch the body.
        more: kata hint 01 http-error

The arc

#ChapterYou prove
01Talk to the modelrequest shape, SSE reassembly, framing, errors, cancellation
02Tool callingtool-call fragments folded by index, ids omitted on continuations
03Tools that touch diskread, write, bash honour the schema, errors, truncation
04The agent loopevent order, one result per call, clean termination
05Prompt assemblyAGENTS.md discovery and attribution
06SessionsJSONL append, replay, resume, idempotence
07Context budgeta hard ceiling, no orphaned pairs, marked pruning, recall
08Steer and abortabort mid-stream, a queued message entering at the seam
09Skillsfrontmatter, lazy body load, arguments, stacking
10Subagentfresh context, scoped tools, exactly one result
11MCP (advanced)stdio JSON-RPC, initialize, tools/list, tools/call

Chapter 11 is optional. Chapters 01 to 04 give you a working agent you can point at Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

When the arc is done, chapters/where-next.md lists what to build on top: recovery of pruned context, a schema budget, parallel tool calls, a second wire format, and the bigger structural changes after those.

What each chapter contains

FileRead whenContains
overview.mdbefore you starthow the mechanism works, with diagrams
problem.mdat the keyboardthe task, the graded claims, the hint ladder
example.mdafter an attempta full annotated implementation

problem.md states every claim the verifier makes, by case id. If a claim and a case ever disagree, the case is correct and the page is a bug.

Commands

kata                      status: current chapter, next action
kata submit [NN]          compile, grade, record
kata submit NN --solution grade the reference instead of your code
kata read [NN] [doc]      problem (default), overview, example
kata hint NN <case-id>    three rungs, from nudge to answer
kata list                 the arc, grouped into parts
kata progress             what passed, and when
kata verify               prove each chapter rejects its starter and accepts its reference
kata reset [NN]           restore agent/ to the state before a chapter
kata read where-next      what to build after the course
kata site                 render the course as a static website in site/dist
kata ui                   terminal interface: pick a chapter, grade it
kata watch [NN]           re-grade on every save
kata doctor               check the environment

kata site writes plain HTML and one stylesheet. Open site/dist/index.html directly, or serve the directory. Diagrams load from a CDN; offline, the diagram source stays readable in place.

How it works

Every chapter leaves you with a program you can run. Chapter 01 gives you an application that answers a prompt; chapter 04 gives you one that completes a multi-step task; chapter 09 one that follows skills you write.

The checks build ./agent/cmd/agent, start a scripted server, point OPENAI_BASE_URL at it, and run your binary. They assert on stdout, stderr, exit codes, and the requests your program sent. Nothing imports your package, so the internal design is yours.

OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1 ./agent -p "list the files here"

Design notes, diagrams, and the grading pipeline are in docs/architecture.md. The chapter file contract is in docs/chapter-format.md.

Requirements

Go 1.26 or newer.

The agent you build uses only the standard library, and keeps doing so through all eleven chapters. The kata tool itself depends on Bubble Tea and Lip Gloss for the terminal interface. That is the whole dependency list, and it belongs to the tool, not to your code.

What Kata is not

Kata teaches the machine, not every attachment. It does not ship a terminal UI, an extension runtime, an LSP client, provider authentication, image input, or a cloud runner. Chapter 11 covers MCP because the client is small enough to teach. For a full harness, read pi, crush, and PiG.

Publishing

The site is committed, so a deploy never needs Go or a browser on the build machine.

kata site --diagrams=render   # writes site/dist, pre-renders every diagram
git add site/dist && git commit -m "site: rebuild"

Netlify serves site/dist through netlify.toml. To deploy by hand:

netlify deploy --prod --dir site/dist

Contributing

A chapter is done when kata verify is clean: its reference passes every case and its starter fails at least one. Hints are validated in both directions, so a case without a ladder fails the test suite. Prose follows docs/writing-style.md.
